propositions: Hand-rolled CLI argument parsing in claim.py and transition.py must be replaced with stdlib argparse while preserving all observable command behavior and sentinel values (None-vs-empty-string for --assignee, None-vs-empty-vs-reason for --force)

The --force flag carries command-specific semantics: claim bare --force consumes following non-option token as reason (else '(no reason given)'), while transition bare --force sets force_reason to empty string without consuming following tokens
The --assignee flag must preserve None-vs-empty-string distinction: absent means use default_assignee fallback, explicit empty string clears the assignee, and value-less at end exits with code 1

Unknown/extra tokens must be silently skipped, --help must remain byte-exact from dispatcher golden files, abbreviations must be disabled, and retired --force-close must continue to exit 1 with existing rejection message
External direct callers of transition._parse_flags (three test modules) must continue to work unchanged with the identical 5-tuple return signature and None-vs-empty-string semantics
Module size and cyclomatic complexity ratchets must be respected; _parse_flags complexity baseline entry must be drained after dropping below threshold
